negative_reviews.author: Isa Sharrocks
negative_reviews.text: Ordered 2 chicken ramen + rainbow sushi roll, watched about 4 tables who came after us get their food. took 30 min until it turned out we was told our order wasnt put through, reordered and waited another 10/15 min until it came. Was got told we'd get a discount for such a long wait only for it to turn out its the 10% off that we would've already have gotten for NHS discount...food was alright, staff friendly.

issues: The site reopened on Friday 30/10 after the fire closure and had a tough first weekend with very low footfall (England KPI meeting 03/11).
On Saturday night (Halloween) youths set off fireworks near the doors and police closed roads, so the site closed early at about 8:30pm and Sunday was very slow (England KPI meeting 03/11).
Matthew reported reopening sales of about £20,300 (Friday £7.1K, Saturday £8.4K, Sunday £4.7K) with labour at 39.93%, linked to the deep cleaning before reopening (Admin Meeting 02/11).
Spencer said labour ran at about 60% because of overstaffing, so floor and bar staffing and hours have been cut back (England KPI meeting 03/11).
Food cost was very high because supplies were bought from Manchester, and should come back down next week (England KPI meeting 03/11).

Sales are well below pre closure levels, also hit by Flat Iron opening nearby; Spencer proposed a £5 ramen for two to three days, but Inka set the priority on labour, customer service and food quality rather than new promotions (England KPI meeting 03/11).

Google reviews: twenty 5 star, nine 4 star and one 2 star about a wait for food after an order was entered wrongly and confusion over a 10% discount (GM/HC meeting 02/11), which pulled the rating to 4.7 (England KPI meeting 03/11).
Inka asked the team to focus on the basics: replying to emails, disputing delivery refunds and updating rotas on Kobas (England KPI meeting 03/11).
The site is short of kimonos (England KPI meeting 03/11).

Staff attitude after the long break was very good, rotas need to be built with the rota tool because some days were very high, deep cleans must be kept up after the shutdown and smoke damage, and the KP wash sink needs fixing (GM/HC meeting 02/11).
A sushi chef is needed urgently (GM/HC meeting 02/11).

The smoke smell is improving after cleaning spray but is not fully gone (Admin Meeting 02/11); before reopening, deep cleaning was 95% done and the Sakura area smell was rated 7 out of 10 (Birmingham Project Meeting 30/10).
Before reopening, JFC deliveries were inconsistent and the printer and PDQ issues were resolved (Birmingham Project Meeting 30/10).
Birmingham ads are restarting with the new opening video and a budget boost (DPM meeting 03/11).
Food cost was high because damaged stock had to be replaced for the reopening, and labour is being adjusted in line with sales (AM Updates 04/11).
The Christmas market in front of the shop should lift footfall, and B2B work is restarting, including a cocktail masterclass at a shared office (AM Updates 04/11).
